name: Tadashi Yanai

name: Gordon Moore
notes: BOUNDED rev10. The Computer History Museum's Fairchild chronology (Corporate Histories Project, semiconductor sector) brackets the constant-dollar crossing from both sides: FSC sales reached approximately $500,000 in 1958 (year-end employment 165, up from 20), below the 1958 nominal bar of $897,674; and Fairchild Camera's 1960 results record that 'Semiconductor contributed approximately $21 million' of FC&I's $67.9M net sales, far above the 1960 bar of $919,417. name: Bong Joon-ho
notes: a5: Memories of Murder (2003) sold over five million tickets; his 2000 feature debut did not reach 1M. a2: Yonsei 1995 per Wikipedia, but other sources say 1994 and his Korean Academy of Film Arts graduation film is dated 1994 - conf lowered. a3: 1994 cinematography credit on a short is the earliest industry work found; the first clearly paid role is assistant director on Motel Cactus (1997), which would move a3 three years. name: Mary Meeker
notes: RE-CODED fund100 -> rank1 under the revised frame. name: Kevin Systrom

name: Robin Li
notes: PINNED, not bounded. SEC EDGAR was reachable this time (curl with a declared User-Agent; the fetch tool still 403s), so the audited statement of operations in Baidu's F-1 supplied the 2003 row the summary table omits: total revenues RMB11,020K (2002), RMB40,571K (2003), RMB117,451K (2004); total net revenues RMB10,524K / RMB38,638K / RMB110,909K, the last stated as US$13.4M. First hit is therefore 2004 exactly, not the 2003-2004 window the first pilot could not resolve, and not the 2005 NASDAQ IPO. Row un-excluded.

name: Daniel Ek
notes: a2: last completed credential is the 2002 IT-Gymnasiet diploma; he left KTH after eight weeks the same year, so dropout and credential coincide. a3: year he joined the SEO firm Jajja not stated in any source found - unknown after two attempts. a4: Advertigo predates Spotify but its founding year is nowhere stated, so a4 records the earliest documented founding (Spotify AB, 2006) at low confidence. a5: Spotify Ltd's first year of trading, revenue GBP11.3M (~$18M); GBP-to-USD conversion is a judgment the frame does not specify. Spotify Ltd's GBP11.3M for 2009 converts at the 2009 average spot rate of 1.566 USD/GBP to about $17.7M, well clear. name: Zhang Yin
notes: RE-CODED excluded -> rank1 under the trade bucket's volume-ranking rule. Two third-party sources, independent of the company, put America Chung Nam first on the Journal of Commerce / PIERS Top 100 US Exporters ranking (by containerized volume, TEU) in 2001 and name 2001 as the first such year. (1) Recycling Today, Brian Taylor, 'Setting sail', 1 June 2002: ACN 'ranked as the number one U.S. exporter by volume in 2001, according to the U.S. Journal of Commerce' - contemporaneous, and it attributes the ranking to JOC rather than to ACN. (2) JOC itself, 27 May 2011: ACN 'was the largest American exporter of containerized goods by volume in 2010 for the 10th year in a row, according to the latest Journal of Commerce Top 100 Importers and Exporters annual rankings' (300,800 TEU in 2010) - a 10-year streak ending 2010 starts in 2001, so JOC's own wording places the first top finish in 2001 and rules out 2000. https://web.archive.org/web/20081201211700/http://www.thefreelibrary.com/Setting+sail%3a+exporting+recovered+paper+to+mills+in+China+is+the...-a087857748 . ACN's own site claims only that it has been 'recognized as a top American exporter to China since 2001' with no ranking body named; that self-description is NOT what this anchor rests on. rev10 remains undatable for both ACN and Nine Dragons (no revenue published before the 2006 HKEX listing, whose turnover table starts at 2003), which is why rank1 applies. a2/a3 stay unknown: sources say she trained in accounting at a trade school and worked as a bookkeeper, then at a Shenzhen paper trading firm, but give no years, after two attempts in the second pilot.

name: Stephanie Shirley
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: BusinessCloud's obituary (11 Aug 2025) states 'Her generosity would see Dame Stephanie drop out of the Sunday Times Rich List', which places her on it before the giving; several accounts call her the first person to leave the list through philanthropy. https://businesscloud.co.uk/news/tech-pioneer-dame-stephanie-steve-shirley-dies-aged-91/ BOUNDED rev10, both ends sourced. Lower end: heise online's obituary prints the early turnover series - 1964 GBP7,000, 1970 GBP50,000, 1976 GBP739,000, 'crossed the million-pound threshold' in 1977, GBP10m in 1987. GBP739,000 at the 1976 average spot rate of about 1.80 USD/GBP is roughly US$1.33M, below the 1976 nominal bar of $1,767,394. Upper end: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F_International, sourced to the Harvard Business School case (Franklin, 1986) and Let IT Go, states that by the end of the 1970s revenue had risen to GBP2.5m; at the 1979 average of about 2.12 USD/GBP that is about US$5.3M, well above the 1979 bar of $2,255,058. The conclusion is insensitive to the exact rate: the 1976 figure needs 2.39 USD/GBP to clear its bar and the 1979 figure clears its own even at parity. NOT PINNED TO 1977 on purpose: the constant-dollar bar in sterling is about GBP1.08m in 1977, GBP1.06m in 1978 and GBP1.06m in 1979, so heise's 'crossed the million-pound threshold in 1977' straddles the bar - GBP1.0m is below it, GBP1.2m above it - and the source gives no figure. The crossing is therefore bounded 1976-1979 rather than dated 1977. No IPO/acq fallback was available anyway: the March 1996 LSE float is 17-20 years late and the frame bars it here. a2: Wikipedia's honours-and-legacy section gives BSc 1956; no other source dates the degree, and 'six years of evening classes' from 1951 would suggest 1957, so conf is medium. a3: Archives of IT's timeline, 'began her IT career at the Post Office in London in 1951 at the age of 18'. a4: 1962 Freelance Programmers, per the F International article; the Steve Shirley article's phrasing around her 1959 marriage has led some obituaries to print 1959 for the founding, which is wrong. a6: March 1996 flotation on the London Stock Exchange.

name: Judy Faulkner
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: her Forbes profile carries a self-made score of 8, inside the roster's 6-10 band, and contemporaneous news reports of the Forbes 400 name her - she entered the 2012 Forbes 400 at No. 285 with $1.7B and ranked No. 154 in 2024. https://www.forbes.com/profile/judy-faulkner/ BOUNDED rev10, both ends sourced, and NO FALLBACK EXISTS: Epic has never listed and has never been acquired, so ipo/acq50 are unavailable and a bounded rev10 is the only legal anchor. Lower end: Acquired's Epic briefing states the company reached '$1.5 million in revenue by 1988', below the 1988 nominal bar of $3,674,564 (41% of it). Upper end: the International Directory of Company Histories entry states 'In 1997, Epic earned net income of $6.6 million on sales of $30.9 million', 6.2x the 1997 bar of $4,985,355. https://www.referenceforbusiness.com/history2/65/Epic-Systems-Corporation.html Span 1988-1997 is nine years, inside the ten-year limit. NARROWER READING NOT USED: a figure of '$18 million in 1995, up from $1.5 million in 1988' is widely repeated and would tighten the bound to 1988-1995, but two fetch attempts (acquired.fm episode page, company-histories.com / jrank mirrors of the same directory entry) failed to surface it on a page I could read, so it is not relied on. Employee counts from the same directory entry are consistent with a crossing in the early 1990s - 30 staff in 1990, 49 in 1993, 125 in 1995 against $155K of revenue per head in 1997 - but headcount times an assumed revenue-per-head is an inference, not a source, so it did not narrow the bound. a2: UNKNOWN after several attempts. Sources conflict and none pins the year: the UW-Madison CS department page lists the M.S. with no year, Forbes says she started a doctorate in 1965 and 'graduated without completing a dissertation' in the early 1970s, and The Capital Times says she founded Epic in 1979 'shortly after receiving her master's degree'. a3: JUDGMENT CALL - Forbes dates her first healthcare-computing work to 1969, the punch-card on-call scheduling system built for Dr John Greist, which is a graduate project rather than paid employment; her first clearly paid domain role, with a University of Wisconsin physicians group, is dated only to 'the early 1970s'. Confidence low. a6: Forbes named her a billionaire in March 2012, the same year she entered the Forbes 400.

name: Dietmar Hopp
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: Forbes' billionaires profile ranks him #634 in the world with $6.4B and lists 'Source of Wealth: Software, Self Made'; German Wikipedia records rank #147 on the 2018 Forbes World's Billionaires list. https://www.forbes.com/profile/dietmar-hopp/ BOUNDED rev10, both ends sourced, IPO FALLBACK BARRED (SAP's 1988 flotation is six to twelve years after the crossing and the earlier crossing is documented). Lower end: SAP's own corporate history page for 1972-1980 states for 1976 'SAP now employs 25 people and generates DM3.81 million in revenue'. At the 1976 annual average of 2.5182 DM/US$ that is US$1.513M, below the 1976 nominal bar of $1,767,394 (86% of it). The margin is not large, but the D-Mark traded in a 2.36-2.62 band through 1976 and the figure would need a rate at or below 2.156 DM/US$ to clear the bar, so the classification holds across the whole year's range. Upper end: Computerwoche's SAP history, 'Zum zehnten Geburtstag 1982 zaehlt SAP bereits ueber 250 Firmenkunden und erzielt einen Umsatz von rund 24 Millionen Mark'; at the 1982 average of 2.4266 DM/US$ that is US$9.89M, 3.3x the 1982 bar of $2,997,425. Span 1976-1982 is six years. NOT NARROWED: SAP's own page says the company had about 60 employees by 1978 and was 'one of Germany's largest software firms', which is a qualitative claim of scale with no figure attached - under the frame that is enough to bar the IPO fallback but not enough to pin a year, and scaling 1976 revenue-per-head onto the 1978 headcount would be an inference, not a source. CONFLICTING SOURCE REJECTED: was-war-wann.de dates the same DM3.8m / small-headcount snapshot to 1980, which contradicts SAP's own 1976 dating, the 1977 Walldorf move, and its own DM24m-with-100-staff figure for 1982; SAP's page and Computerwoche agree on 1976 and were preferred. a2: German Wikipedia, Diplom-Ingenieur in Nachrichtentechnik from TH Karlsruhe in 1966. a3: BOUNDED. No source gives the year he joined IBM. English Wikipedia says 'After graduating from university, he worked as a software developer and consultant at IBM' (so not before the 1966 degree) and German Wikipedia dates his IBM Mannheim systems-consultant post to 1968-1972, so the start is bracketed to 1966-1968 rather than assumed to be 1966. a6: 1988, the year SAP became an AG and listed; Computerwoche gives DM340m of revenue in that first stock-market year.

name: Kazuhiko Nishi
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP UNCONFIRMED. Two searches (Japanese, for 長者番付 / 高額納税者番付 / 日経 and 東洋経済 rankings naming him, and for any Nikkei or Toyo Keizai ranking listing him or ASCII) produced no ranking that names Nishi. Toyo Keizai Online has published a feature ARTICLE about him ('早大1浪2留中退'名家の母を嘆かせた彼の後悔, toyokeizai.net/articles/-/743951) and Nikkei Business has interviewed him, but a bylined article is not a ranking and the roster's claim is not verified. Flagging for the reviewer rather than dropping the row. PINNED rev10, not bounded. Yamazaki Yasuo's Hosei University RIIM working paper No.24 ('パソコン黎明期のベンチャー・ビジネス - 椎名堯慶と西和彦', Japanese business-history series No.41) prints ASCII's audited fiscal-year revenue series in 表2 (units 百万円, compiled by the author from 日経新聞社編『会社総鑑』): 1977 40, 1978 142, 1979 353, 1980 835, 1981 1,634, 1982 4,200, 1983 5,047, 1984 7,756, 1985 13,884. Both sides of the crossing come from that one table. FY1979 revenue of 353 million yen at the 1979 annual average of 219.14 yen/US$ is US$1.61M, below the 1979 nominal bar of $2,255,058 (71% of it). FY1980 revenue of 835 million yen at the 1980 average of 226.74 yen/US$ is US$3.68M, above the 1980 bar of $2,559,459 (144% of it). The call is robust to the rate: 1979 would need a rate of 156.5 yen/US$ to clear its bar and 1980 would need 326 yen/US$ to fall below its own, and the yen traded roughly 194-251 in 1979 and 203-264 in 1980. The 1989 flotation is nine years late and barred. CAVEAT: en.wikipedia's ASCII article says 'In 1980, ASCII made 1.2 billion yen of sales from licensing Microsoft BASIC', which exceeds the whole-company 835 million yen in the table - most likely a calendar-year or ASCII-Microsoft-inclusive figure, since ASCII Microsoft KK was a separate 1978 entity not merged into ASCII until 1984. Either reading puts 1980 above the bar; the risk it carries is that a consolidated 1979 figure might also have cleared, which is why confidence is medium rather than high. a2: 1974, his graduation from Koyo Gakuin High School, which is the last credential he COMPLETED before his career - the same convention used for p09 Daniel Ek. He entered Waseda's mechanical engineering department in 1975 and never graduated: the working paper's chronology dates his mid-course withdrawal to 1983, three years after the crossing, and ja.wikipedia records the withdrawal with no year (Toyo Keizai calls him '1浪2留中退'). Recording that 1983 withdrawal as a2 would put education_end after first_hit, which is factually what happened but is not what this anchor measures. A doctorate from Kogakuin University followed in 1999, twenty years into his career, and is likewise not used. a4: 1976, the launch of the monthly I/O in November of that year, which the paper treats as the venture he and the later ASCII founders ran before splitting off; Nishi's own CV at nishi.org independently dates his first company, Pax Electronica, to 1976. ASCII Publishing itself was founded in May 1977 and is the hit entity. a3: no domain employment ever preceded his own ventures, so a3 is set equal to a4 at low confidence under the p01 rule; the paper describes him writing articles for the magazine コンピュートピア as an undergraduate, which would be earlier but is given no year.

name: Sandra Kurtzig
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP UNCONFIRMED. Two attempts (a direct search for 'Sandra Kurtzig' with 'Forbes 400', and a search of her net-worth coverage) found no source placing her on the Forbes 400. The arithmetic points the other way: her personal stake in ASK was worth about $65-67M in 1981-1983, and Wikipedia's Forbes 400 article records that the inaugural 1982 list required $75M to make it, a bar that rose in later years - so she was probably just under the cut in the only years her wealth peaked. She is repeatedly described as the first woman to take a Silicon Valley technology company public and appeared on Forbes and Fortune covers, which may be what the roster claim was built on. Flagging for the reviewer, not dropping the row. BOUNDED rev10, IPO FALLBACK BARRED. Upper end: the Gale/Encyclopedia.com biography states 'Between 1979 and 1983, sales soared from $2.8 million to $39 million'. ASK's $2.8M in 1979 is above the 1979 nominal bar of $2,255,058 (124% of it), so the crossing is 1979 or earlier and the October 1981 IPO - two or more years late - cannot be used. Lower end: the frame's founding-year rule. ASK was started in 1972 with a $2,000 GE commission check and cannot have earned before it existed, and at seven years old at the crossing it is exactly the young-entity case the rule is written for. Span 1972-1979 is seven years, inside the limit. NOT NARROWED, and this is the weak part of the row: two further attempts (a targeted search for 1976-1978 dollar figures, and the EBSCO biography) turned up no revenue figure for any year before 1979, so the bound cannot be tightened even though the qualitative record - MANMAN shipped to Hughes in January 1976 and 'took off' from 1978 - suggests the true crossing sits at the 1978-1979 end of the window. Confidence low on that account: the midpoint the clocks will use, 1975.5, is probably three years early. a1: Wikipedia gives 21 October 1947; the EBSCO biography prints 1946 in its overview and 1947 in its body - conflict, conf medium. a2: BS mathematics, UCLA, 1968, per Wikipedia citing American Men & Women of Science. She also holds a Stanford master's in aeronautical engineering, but no source found gives its year, so the last credential with a sourced year is used. a3: BOUNDED. Her GE computer time-sharing sales job has no sourced start year; the UCLA degree (1968) brackets it from below and Wikipedia's 'In 1972, she left her job selling computer time-sharing for General Electric' brackets it from above. a6: the 1981 IPO, retained as the scale marker it properly is.

name: Shola Akinlade
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED (with one caveat). YC's own company page confirms Paystack as a Y Combinator W2016 alum with status 'Acquired' (https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/paystack), and YC's published Top Companies criterion admits exits valued above $150M, which the $200M+ Stripe deal clears; search indexing of ycombinator.com/topcompanies/valuation/exits places Paystack at position 33. The Top Companies page itself renders client-side and could not be fetched directly, so the listing is corroborated rather than read off the page. FALLBACK USED, AND THE BAR ON IT WAS CHECKED. Stripe acquired Paystack in October 2020 for a reported $200M+ (TechCrunch, Reuters), far above the 2020 acq50 bar of $40,195,159. The frame bars the fallback whenever an earlier rev10 crossing is known; two attempts found no revenue figure for Paystack in any year, and the volume record argues against an earlier crossing rather than for one. Paystack's own blog milestone puts monthly transaction VALUE at 10 billion naira around September 2018 (about US$27.5M at the ~360 naira/US$ rate of that year); at Paystack's published local-card pricing of 1.5% plus 100 naira capped at 2,000 naira, that volume annualises to roughly US$4-5M of gross revenue, below the 2018 bar of $7,799,735. That arithmetic is an estimate and is used only to test whether the fallback is barred - it dates nothing. Nairametrics (Sept 2018) puts Paystack at 17,000 businesses and 'over 15% of all online payments in Nigeria', which is a real business but not the 'already industry-leading' claim that would bar the fallback; the 'more than half of all online transactions in Nigeria' and 60,000-merchant descriptions are stated as of the October 2020 acquisition itself. If Paystack's 2020 revenue did clear the $8,039,032 bar for that year, the anchor year would be 2020 under rev10 as well, so the fallback is not moving the date - the same structure as p07 Instagram. a1: no source of record gives his birth date - Wikipedia's infobox leaves it blank - so the row rests on Nigerian biography coverage (legit.ng) giving 3 March 1985; conf low. a2: BSc computer science, Babcock University, 2006 (Wikipedia, citing Nairametrics). a3: Heineken management trainee in database management, 2007-2009 per Nairametrics; he is also described as later working as a software engineer at several banks, with no years given anywhere. a4: Klein Devort, the software development and consulting company through which Precurio was built - legit.ng dates it to 2009 while other biography pages say 2008, and neither Wikipedia nor Nairametrics mentions the company at all, hence low confidence. Paystack (2015) is the hit entity, not the first venture. a6: UNKNOWN after two attempts - no scale marker after the 2020 acquisition is datable to Akinlade's own venture; the 2022 Officer of the Order of the Niger honour and the Sporting Lagos football club are recognition and a new venture, not a scale hit for Paystack.

name: Shigenobu Nagamori
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: Nikkei's own site prints the ranking. His Nikkei Global Management Forum speaker profile (nikkeiforum.com/ngmf2016jp/speakers09.html) records that he ranked first in Nikkei Business's 2014 survey ranking of best CEOs chosen by company presidents; the Nikkei Business issue of 17 Nov 2014 is the source of the ranking, reported contemporaneously at https://www.excite.co.jp/news/article/Bizjournal_mixi201411_post-2088/ . That is a Nikkei-published ranking, not a feature article, so the roster's 'Nikkei / Toyo Keizai rankings (Japan)' citation holds. BOUNDED rev10, both ends sourced, IPO FALLBACK BARRED (the Nov 1988 Osaka/Kyoto listing is at least nine years after the crossing and Nidec's own history documents the earlier crossing). Upper end: Nidec's official 50-year history, chapter 2, dates the milestone to the fiscal year ended March 1979 - (第6期) 売上高10億円を達成, i.e. 1 billion yen of revenue in the sixth fiscal year. At the 1979 annual average of 219.14 yen/US$ that is US$4.56M, 202% of the 1979 nominal bar of $2,255,058. The fiscal year ended March 1979 actually spans April 1978 to March 1979, so the 1978 reading was checked too: at the 1978 average of 210.44 yen/US$ the same 1 billion yen is US$4.75M against a 1978 bar of $2,025,203, or 235% of it. Above the bar on either reading. Robust to the rate: the yen would have to be weaker than about 443 per US$ for the figure to fall below the 1979 bar, and it traded roughly 194-251 through 1979. Lower end: the frame's founding-year rule. Nidec was incorporated on 23 July 1973 with 20 million yen of capital and four people, and cannot have earned before it existed. Span 1973-1979 is six years, inside the ten-year limit. NOT NARROWED: three attempts (Japanese searches for early-period 売上高 by year, Nidec's IR history pages, and the Diamond Online growth retrospective, which paywalls its revenue chart) found no revenue figure for any year between 1973 and 1978, so the crossing cannot be pinned. The yen bar in those years is about 524M yen (1976), 505M yen (1977) and 426M yen (1978), i.e. roughly half the FY1979 figure, so the true crossing is probably at the 1977-1978 end of the window and the midpoint the clocks will use, 1976, is likely one or two years early. a2: 1967 graduation from the Institute of Vocational Training (職業訓練大学校, now Polytechnic University), electrical engineering, per the Nikkei forum profile; ja.wikipedia adds that the graduation was in March 1967 and top of his class. a3: BOUNDED. ja.wikipedia states he joined the audio-equipment maker Teac after graduating and later became a director of Yamashina Seiki, but no source found gives the year he joined Teac; the March 1967 graduation brackets it from below and the July 1973 founding of Nidec from above. Japanese new-graduate hiring convention makes April 1967 very likely, but that is an inference, so the span is recorded instead. a4: Nidec is also the hit entity; no earlier venture is recorded, and ja.wikipedia notes he funded the founding by selling his Teac shareholding. a6: November 1988 listing on the Osaka Securities Exchange second section and the Kyoto Stock Exchange, fifteen years after founding; Nidec's history gives 25.8 billion yen of revenue for the fiscal year ended March 1988.

name: Morris Chang
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: his Forbes billionaires profile gives Source of Wealth 'Semiconductors, Self Made' and a world rank on the Forbes Billionaires list - $9.9B and #361 real-time as read on 13 Aug 2026, #422 on the published 2026 list with $8.4B. https://www.forbes.com/profile/morris-chang/ JUDGMENT CALL (a4 = TSMC, 1987, not something earlier). frame.md defines the hit criteria but never defines a4_first_venture, so the convention was taken from the completed rows: a4 is the first thing the person FOUNDED, which may precede the hit entity (p02 RNARx before the prize, p14 the I/O magazine venture before ASCII, p16 Klein Devort before Paystack). Nothing Chang did before 1987 was a founding. Sylvania Semiconductor (1955-58), Texas Instruments (1958-83) and General Instrument (1984-85) were employment, however senior - at TI he ran the semiconductor group and later was group vice president, but it was someone else's company. The Industrial Technology Research Institute presidency he took in 1985 is the only real candidate for an earlier a4 and it fails too: ITRI was an existing state-funded research institute founded in 1973 that he was recruited to lead, not a venture he started. Vanguard International Semiconductor, which he did help create and chaired from 1994, is seven years later than TSMC. So a4 = a5's entity = TSMC, February 1987, and the 25-year TI apprenticeship the roster wants measured runs a3 1955 to a4 1987. SECOND JUDGMENT CALL, recorded because it could be read the other way: TSMC was incorporated as a joint venture of the Taiwanese government's development fund, Philips and private Taiwanese investors, with Chang recruited to build and run it, so 'the person's own venture' is not as clean here as it is for Nagamori or Zhou. Forbes treats him as self-made and as TSMC's founder, and every company history names him founding chairman and CEO, so the row treats TSMC as his venture. BOUNDED rev10, both ends sourced, IPO FALLBACK BARRED (the September 1994 Taiwan Stock Exchange listing is at least two years after the crossing, and revenue is documented from before it). Upper end: the International Directory of Company Histories entry, 'Revenue for 1992 was around $245 million' - 44 times the 1992 nominal bar of $4,357,914, so the crossing is 1992 or earlier by a wide margin. No currency conversion is needed; the source states US dollars. Lower end: the frame's founding-year rule. TSMC was incorporated 21 February 1987 and cannot have earned before it existed. Span 1987-1992 is five years. NOT NARROWED, and this is the weak part of the row: three attempts (TSMC's own 30-year milestone pages on investor.tsmc.com, Chinese-language searches of Taiwanese financial media for 1987-1990 營收, and the Our World in Data TSMC revenue series, which starts at 2006) produced no revenue figure for any year from 1987 to 1991. A widely-copied secondary claim that revenue was about NT$100 million at founding would put 1987 at roughly US$3.14M at the 1987 average of about 31.8 NT$/US$, just below the 1987 bar of $3,528,575 - but it appears only on low-quality aggregator pages, the margin is inside the plausible error of the rate and the figure, and it would not move the bound anyway, so it is not relied on. The qualitative record - a rented 6-inch fab in production from 1987, Intel as a customer in 1988, US and European subsidiaries in 1988 and 1989 - suggests the true crossing is at the early end of the window, most likely 1987 or 1988, so the midpoint the clocks will use, 1989.5, is probably one to two years late. a2: 1964, the Stanford PhD in electrical engineering, taken on leave with TI's sponsorship and therefore nine years AFTER a3. That is what the anchor literally measures, but the competing reading is defensible and is recorded here: his MIT mechanical engineering degrees (BS 1952, MS 1953) are the credentials he actually entered the industry with, and under that reading a2 would be 1953. a3: 1955, Sylvania Semiconductor, his first semiconductor job; he moved to Texas Instruments in 1958. a6: September 1994 Taiwan Stock Exchange listing, with 1994 sales of $744 million; the April 1996 NYSE listing, the first by a Taiwanese company, is the later alternative.

name: Zhou Qunfei
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: she tops the 2015 Hurun Women Rich List, reported by China News Service (https://www.chinanews.com/cj/2015/10-19/7577560.shtml) and CNR - 45岁的周群飞以财富500亿元成为新一届女首富, and Hurun also named her the world's richest self-made woman that year. She appears on the main 2015 胡润百富榜 as well (wiki.mbalib.com/wiki/2015胡润百富榜, the Zhou Qunfei / Zheng Junlong couple entry), so the roster's 'Hurun Rich List (China)' citation holds on the main list and not merely the women's variant. BOUNDED rev10, both ends sourced, IPO FALLBACK BARRED (the 18 March 2015 ChiNext listing is roughly a decade after the crossing and revenue is documented from well before it). Upper end: the Sina Finance republication of the 36Kr company retrospective states 蓝思的营收从千万级跃升至2006年10亿元级别 - revenue jumped from the tens-of-millions level to the order of 1 billion yuan in 2006, after the Motorola V3 cover-glass win. At the 2006 annual average of 7.97 RMB/US$ that is about US$125M, twenty times the 2006 nominal bar of $6,261,978. The figure is an order-of-magnitude statement rather than an audited number, but nothing inside its error bar comes near the bar: it would have to be wrong by a factor of twenty to matter. Lower end: the frame's founding-year rule. Shenzhen Lens Technology was founded in July 2003 (zh.wikipedia, 深圳的蓝思科技始建于2003年7月) and cannot have earned before it existed. Span 2003-2006 is three years. NOT NARROWED: the same source's earlier bracket, 千万级 (tens of millions of yuan), straddles the bar rather than sitting below it - the constant-dollar bar in yuan is about 47.3M yuan in 2003, 48.6M in 2004 and 49.7M in 2005, i.e. inside the 10-99M range that 千万级 denotes - so it cannot pin a side. Three attempts (Chinese searches for 2003-2005 营收, the ChiNext prospectus route via Sina and cninfo, which only reaches back to 2011, and the Hunan/Zhihu company histories, which 403) produced no year-by-year figure before 2006. JUDGMENT CALL, and the main risk in this row: the hit entity is taken to be Lens Technology (founded 2003), not the 1993 predecessor workshop, so 2003 rather than 1993 is the legal lower bound. If the two were treated as one continuous business the bracket would be 1993-2006, sixteen years, over the ten-year limit, and the row would have to be excluded as crossing_undatable. The separation is defensible: 恒生玻璃表面加工厂, founded 18 March 1993, was a different product (watch glass, not phone cover glass), a different legal entity, and is consistently described as a family workshop of eight people that grew to a few dozen; Zhou's own account in the Economic Observer is 从1993年创业至2002年近10年，我的财富才只有百万级别 - through 2002 her wealth was only in the millions of yuan - which is a qualitative claim that the predecessor never approached the bar. It is a wealth statement, not a revenue figure, which is why confidence here is low. a1: 1970 per zh.wikipedia; no source of record gives a full date and coverage disagrees on her age at each milestone, so conf is medium. a2: 1987, the year she left school. The Economic Observer states 1987年，上到初二的时候...17岁的她...开启了外来妹之旅 - she left during the second year of junior high in 1987. Other coverage says she left at 15, which against a 1970 birth would put the year at 1985-86; the year 1987 is the only one any source states, so it is used and the age conflict is what holds confidence at medium. She later took night classes at Shenzhen University in accounting and computing while working, but no source dates them, so they are not used. a3: 1987, the same year - line worker at the Aoya Optical watch-glass factory in Shenzhen, i.e. glass surface processing, the same domain as the eventual hit. a4: 18 March 1993, 恒生玻璃表面加工厂, started with HK$20,000 of savings in a rented Bao'an apartment; this is the first venture, not the hit entity. a6: the March 2015 ChiNext listing, which took her to the top of the Hurun women's list overnight.

name: An Wang
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED, WITH THE CAVEAT THE BRIEF FLAGS. The Gale biographical entry states he was estimated to be the fifth richest man in America by Forbes magazine in 1984, which is the Forbes 400 of September 1984; UPI's contemporaneous wire report on that list (upi.com/Archives/1984/09/17/The-Forbes-400-richest-Americans-Oil-electronics-and-rock-n-roll/2727464241600/, 403 to a direct fetch but indexed and quoted) names him among the 21 immigrants on it at $1.6B. CAVEAT: Forbes did not publish a self-made SCORE until the 2010s, so the roster's '(self-made score 6-10)' qualifier cannot be verified for a 1984 edition. In substance the qualifier is safe - he arrived in the US in 1945 with no capital and started the company with $600 - but no score exists to cite. PINNED rev10, not bounded, and both sides come from the same source. The International Directory of Company Histories entry for Wang Laboratories gives 'The first truly successful year for the Linasec machine was 1963, when the company recorded $300,000 in sales' and, of the following year, 'allowing Wang in fiscal 1964 to exceed $1 million in sales for the first time'. THE CONSTANT-DOLLAR CHECK IS WHAT MAKES THIS ROW WORK AND ALSO WHERE IT IS THINNEST. The 1963 nominal bar is $950,479 and $300,000 is 32% of it - clearly below. The 1964 nominal bar is $962,903 and the source says sales exceeded $1,000,000 - above, but by only about 4%. en.wikipedia's An Wang article independently gives '1964: sales reached $1,000,000', the same figure. So the crossing is dated 1964 rather than the $10M-nominal year, which Wang Laboratories did not see until 1970 ('In 1970, the huge success of calculators helped the company record its first year of $25 million in sales') - a nominal reading would have put this row six years late. BLUNT ABOUT THE MARGIN: a 4% overstatement in a round '$1 million' - i.e. a true figure anywhere below $962,903 - would move the anchor to 1965, so confidence is medium, not high. The direction of the fiscal-year ambiguity was checked and does not matter: Wang's fiscal 1964 spans mid-1963 to mid-1964, and $1M clears the 1963 bar of $950,479 as well as the 1964 bar, while the $300,000 figure is below both. NO EARLIER CROSSING: the same entry describes the company in the last two years of the 1950s as about 20 employees producing 60 to 80 units a year at about $700 each, roughly $50,000 of annual sales against a bar near $900,000, so nothing before 1963 comes close. IPO FALLBACK NOT USED AND BARRED ANYWAY: the 1967 NYSE offering of 210,000 shares is three years after the crossing. a2: Harvard PhD in applied physics, 1948, after the MS in 1946; he enrolled in September 1945. a3: JUDGMENT CALL - 1941, when he volunteered with eight classmates to design and build transmitters and radios for Nationalist troops and worked at the Central Radio Works in Kweilin (Guilin), aged 21. That is electronics hardware engineering, the same broad domain as the eventual venture, and it is his first paid technical work after the 1940 Chiao Tung degree and a year as a teaching assistant. The competing reading is 1948, when he joined Howard Aiken's Harvard Computation Laboratory and invented the magnetic core memory write-after-read cycle, which is the first COMPUTING job specifically; that reading would shorten the a3-to-a5 clock by seven years. Confidence medium for that reason, and note that a2 (1948) therefore falls after a3 (1941), which is factually correct - the wartime work preceded the American degrees. a4: June 1951, Wang Laboratories, founded as a sole proprietorship with $600 after Harvard cut back its computer research; incorporated 1955. No earlier venture is recorded. a6: the 1967 New York Stock Exchange offering.

name: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED on Hurun's own site: the Hurun India Rich List 2014 page at hurun.net (https://www.hurun.net/en-us/info/detail?num=9E4ADEB6CB3D) ranks her 100th at INR 6,500 crore and calls her 'the only self made woman in the list'. She is still on it a decade later - the M3M Hurun India Rich List 2025 places her 107th at INR 29,330 crore and fourth among self-made women, reported by Business Today (https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/m3m-hurun-india-rich-list-2025-hcls-roshni-nadar-bags-third-rank-on-debut-becomes-wealthiest-woman-496511-2025-10-01). This is a ranking, not a feature article, so the roster's citation holds. EXCLUDED, crossing_undatable, and the reason is the LOWER end of the bracket, not the upper. Upper end is available: Biocon's revenue is repeatedly reported as Rs 70 crore in 1998 (blog.shoonya.com/biocon-company/ and mynation.com, both tracing the same 'Rs 70 crore in 1998 to Rs 500 crore at the 2004 IPO' claim). At the 1998 average of about 41.3 INR/US$ that is US$16.9M, 335% of the 1998 nominal bar of $5,063,008 - above the bar even if the figure is halved. Lower end is what fails. The frame's founding-year rule gives 1978 (incorporated 29 November 1978, per Biocon's own legacy page), and 1978-1998 is a twenty-year span, double the ten-year limit. Nothing narrows it: SIX attempts (Biocon's current legacy page and the archived archive.biocon.com history page, the 2004 annual report, which prints only FY2001-FY2004; the 2004 IPO prospectus at archive.biocon.com/docs/IPO.pdf, which is a scanned image with no extractable text; the MIT Sloan 'Biocon India Group' case, which gives only US$75M of revenue around 2002; the WIPO IP Advantage case study, whose earliest figure is 2010; and repeated English-language searches for 1980s and early-1990s turnover) produced NO revenue figure for any year between 1978 and 1997. IPO FALLBACK BARRED: the July 2004 listing is at least six years after the crossing, and the qualitative record - profitable by the time Auchincloss sold to Unilever in 1989 (britannica.com/money/Kiran-Mazumdar-Shaw), India's leading enzyme producer by the mid-1990s, a three-fold plant expansion in 1996 - establishes an earlier crossing under the frame's 'what known means' rule. So the row is excluded rather than dated by the IPO. FOR THE RECORD, the constant-dollar bar in rupees is much lower than intuition suggests: Rs 4.1 crore in 1985, Rs 7.1 crore in 1990, Rs 15.4 crore in 1995. An enzyme exporter running a 20-acre Hosur Road plant from 1983 plausibly crossed in the late 1980s, but plausibly is not sourced, and dating it would be exactly the defect this project exists to prevent. a1: born 23 March 1953 in Bangalore. a2: 1975, Master Brewer, Ballarat College / University of Melbourne, after the 1973 BSc in zoology from Bangalore University; conf medium because the 1975 degree and the 1975 first job are given the same year by en.wikipedia and other coverage puts the Carlton training in 1974. a3: 1975, trainee brewer at Carlton and United Breweries, Melbourne - fermentation science, the same domain as Biocon's brewing enzymes, and her first paid technical work; the competing reading is 1978 (Biocon itself) if 'domain' is read as biotech rather than fermentation, which would collapse a3 into a4. a4: 29 November 1978, Biocon India Pvt Ltd, seed capital Rs 10,000, a JV in which Indian foreign-ownership rules left her holding 70%; it is also the hit entity, and no earlier venture is recorded. a6: the 2004 IPO, which closed at a market value of US$1.1 billion on day one.

name: Thomas Struengmann
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: his Forbes billionaire profile (https://www.forbes.com/profile/thomas-struengmann/) gives a world rank - #314 real-time as read on 13 Aug 2026 - with $11.1B and Source of Wealth 'Pharmaceuticals, Self Made', Germany. That is the ranking itself, not a feature article, so the roster's citation holds. The roster cites the list without a self-made score, so no score needs verifying. BOUNDED rev10, both ends sourced, and the fallback never arises because no IPO exists - Hexal stayed private until the 2005 Novartis sale. Upper end: the International Directory of Company Histories entry for Hexal AG, 'By 1988, the company's revenues had topped the equivalent of EUR 28 million.' The source states the euro equivalent of a D-mark figure at the fixed 1.95583 DM/EUR conversion, i.e. DM 54.8M; at the 1988 annual average of 1.7562 DM/US$ that is US$31.2M, 849% of the 1988 nominal bar of $3,674,564. The margin is enormous and rate-insensitive: the D-mark would have to trade above 14.9 per US$ for DM 54.8M to fall below the bar, against an actual 1988 range near 1.66-1.88. Lower end: the frame's founding-year rule. Hexal Chemie GmbH & Co. KG was established in 1986 in Tegernsee, Bavaria, with five drug preparations and 22 employees, and cannot have earned before it existed. Span 1986-1988 is two years, the tightest bound in this bucket. NOT NARROWED, but the direction is knowable: the same source gives first-month sales equivalent to EUR 220,000 (DM 430,283, US$198,150 at the 1986 average of 2.1715 DM/US$). Twelve months at that rate would be US$2.38M against a 1986 bar of $3,404,329, and 1986 was a partial year in any case, so the crossing is very probably 1987 - which is also the midpoint the clocks will use. That reasoning is not sourced arithmetic about an actual 1986 total, so it does not move the bound; two further attempts (German searches for Hexal Umsatz 1987/1989 and the de.wikipedia Hexal AG article, which carries no revenue figures at all) found no annual figure between 1986 and 1988. The constant-dollar bar in D-marks for reference: DM 7.39M in 1986, DM 6.34M in 1987, DM 6.45M in 1988 - low enough that a fast-growing generics launch clears it quickly, which is why the window is short. JUDGMENT CALL on the hit entity: Hexal, not Durachemie. Durachemie was their father Ernst Struengmann's Frankfurt pharmaceutical company, which Thomas ran as CEO from 1979 and the family sold to Cyanamid in 1986 - an inherited going concern, not his own venture, so its revenue cannot fire the criterion however large it was. Sources also mention that in 1985 the family spun off one of Durachemie's subsidiaries; if that spun-off entity were treated as Hexal's start, the lower bound would move to 1985 and the span to three years, still inside the limit and still bracketing 1987, so nothing in the row turns on it. a1: born 16 February 1950 in Muelheim an der Ruhr, twin of Andreas. a2: 1977, University of Augsburg - the two company-history renderings disagree on whether the 1977 degree was an MBA (fundinguniverse) or a doctorate (encyclopedia.com), and de.wikipedia records a later Dr. rer. pol. on physician prescribing behaviour, but every version agrees on Augsburg in 1977, so the year is high confidence and the degree type is not. a3: BOUNDED 1977-1978, product manager at Schering-Plough. The source brackets it from both sides in one sentence - the 1977 degree, then the job 'initially in Lucerne before transferring to New Jersey in 1978' - so the job began in 1977 or 1978 and no source gives the month. de.wikipedia adds that he distributed pharmaceuticals for his father's firm while still a student, which would be earlier, but it is undated and therefore unusable. a4: 1986, Hexal; the 1979 Durachemie CEO role was a family appointment, not a founding, on the same convention the completed rows use for p03 and p18. a6: the sale of Hexal AG to Novartis, announced February 2005 and completed 7 June 2005, with Hexal folded into Sandoz; Forbes puts the price at about $7 billion, far above the acq50 bar, but rev10 fires roughly eighteen years earlier.

name: Zhong Huijuan
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED on the MAIN Hurun China list, not only the women's variant. The 2025 Hurun Rich List (2025胡润百富榜) places Zhong Huijuan and her daughter Sun Yuan 26th at RMB 130 billion, and the 2024 list placed her 42nd at RMB 77 billion, reported by Sina Finance (https://finance.sina.com.cn/roll/2025-10-30/doc-infvsqmh9263351.shtml and https://finance.sina.com.cn/stock/stockzmt/2024-10-29/doc-incufqpv7623934.shtml). Hurun's own site corroborates on the companion ranking: the 2025 Hurun Richest Women in China page (https://www.hurun.net/zh-cn/info/detail?num=PKHVF5M1TTQX) makes her China's richest woman at RMB 141 billion. Rankings, not feature articles, so the roster's citation holds. EXCLUDED, crossing_undatable, and the gap is the UPPER end. Lower end exists and is unusually good for a private Chinese company: Jiemian's company history states that Hansoh's first flagship product, the cephalexin sustained-release tablet Meifeng, launched in April 1997 and 当年实现收入3000万元 - RMB 30M of revenue that year (https://www.jiemian.com/article/3225325.html; drugtimes.cn/2020/07/28/479aedea22/ gives the same figure). At the 1997 annual average of 8.2898 RMB/US$ that is US$3.62M, 73% of the 1997 nominal bar of $4,985,355 - below the bar, but only by about a quarter, and the figure is the PRODUCT's sales, so company revenue was at least that and could have been over the bar. Even taken at face value it only fixes the lower end. The upper end is the problem. The earliest company-level revenue figure found anywhere is 2011, when Jiemian reports Hansoh's revenue at over RMB 3.5 billion, 78 times the 2011 bar of RMB 45.1M. 1997-2011 is a fourteen-year span and 1995-2011 is sixteen; both exceed the ten-year limit, so no legal bound exists. SEVEN attempts at a figure for 1998-2010: Hansoh's own 发展历程 and 公司简介 pages (milestones only, no revenue); the drugtimes 25-year retrospective (a 2015-2019 chart with no numbers in the text); the Jiangsu CPPCC Lianyungang pharma base paper (gives Hengrui's 2006 revenue of about RMB 1.5bn but nothing for Hansoh); the medvalley history of the Lianyungang cluster (industry aggregates only); Hengrui's 2007 annual report from cninfo, downloaded and searched - it names Jiangsu Hansoh as a related party and discloses RMB 4.23M of material purchases but no Hansoh financials; Chinese searches for the first (2006) China pharmaceutical industry top-100 list, where Hansoh ranked 69th, which never publish its revenue line; and product-level searches for Oulanning (olanzapine) and Zefei (gemcitabine), which return sample-hospital market totals for the whole molecule rather than Hansoh's sales. IPO FALLBACK BARRED: the 14 June 2019 Hong Kong listing is at least eight years after the crossing - Hansoh was already a RMB 3.5bn business in 2011 and entered China's national pharmaceutical top 100 in 2003 - so dating the row by the IPO would be wrong by well over a decade. FOR THE RECORD the bar in yuan is small: RMB 41.3M in 1997, RMB 47.3M in 2003, RMB 49.7M in 2005. A company whose single flagship product did RMB 30M in 1997 and which was a national top-100 pharmaceutical maker by 2003 almost certainly crossed between 1998 and 2001, but no source states it, and guessing inside that window is exactly what this project forbids. a1: born April 1961. a2: July 1982, BSc chemistry, Jiangsu Normal University (a later Nanjing University master's is undated and unused). a3: 1995 and equal to a4, on the p01 convention for career switchers - she taught chemistry at Lianyungang Yan'an Middle School from 1982 and had no pharmaceutical job before the venture; conf medium because some Chinese coverage instead says she resigned from a post at the Lianyungang drug administration rather than from teaching, and no source dates that post. a4: 1995, when the company was set up in Lianyungang (Hansoh's own history page dates the founding of 连云港豪森制药有限公司 to 1995). JUDGMENT CALL: sources agree her husband Sun Piaoyang and an outside investor put the company together in 1995 while he ran the state-owned Lianyungang Pharmaceutical Factory, and that she left teaching to run it as its founder; some accounts date her arrival to 1996 or 1997. The roster treats her as founder and so does this row, but it is the softest part of the identification. a6: the 14 June 2019 listing of Hansoh Pharmaceutical Group on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (03692.HK).

name: Alfred Mann
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED, with the same caveat p20 carries. Forbes ranked him on the Forbes 400: #125 in 2005 (https://images.forbes.com/lists/2005/54/NG0I.html) and #262 in 2008 (https://www.forbes.com/lists/2008/54/400list08_Alfred-Mann_NG0I.html), the ranking pages themselves, not features. CAVEAT: Forbes only began publishing a self-made SCORE in 2014 (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes_400), and Mann died in February 2016, so the roster's '(self-made score 6-10)' qualifier cannot be verified against any edition he appeared on. In substance it is safe - a Portland shopkeeper's son who started his first company on an $11,200 Army contract - but no score exists to cite. SERIAL-FOUNDER JUDGMENT CALL, which is the whole content of this row. The frame dates the FIRST crossing among the person's own ventures, so each company was tested in founding order against the bar for its own years. (1) SPECTROLAB, founded 1956, and HELIOTEK, founded 1960 - his own until Textron bought both in 1960. The bar here is tiny: $844,870 in 1956, $897,674 in 1958, $919,417 in 1960. No revenue figure for either company in any year was found. The only sourced transaction value is contradictory. Joel West's PV-industry working paper, citing the contemporaneous Los Angeles Times report of 2 August 1960 ('Textron Buys Spectrolab of N. Hollywood', p. 23), says Textron paid $300,000 (http://www.joelwest.org/Papers/West2014a-WP.pdf, p. 5) - which is 7% of the 1960 acq50 nominal bar of $4,597,087 and points to revenue below the $919,417 rev10 bar. The International Directory of Company Histories entry for MannKind instead says Textron acquired Spectrolab and Heliotek 'for $11 million', which would be well above the acq50 bar and would imply a rev10 crossing around 1958-1960. I cannot resolve the conflict: the $300,000 figure has the contemporaneous newspaper behind it and fits a company that started on an $11,200 contract four years earlier, while the $11 million figure sits one paragraph away from that same $11,200 in the IDCH text and may be a corruption of it. Under either reading no revenue year can be pinned or bounded from above, so Spectrolab cannot carry the anchor; and after August 1960 it and Heliotek were Textron divisions that Mann ran as an employee until 1972, so their later growth is not 'the person's own venture'. (2) PACESETTER SYSTEMS is where the crossing almost certainly happened. Mann's own bio in MiniMed's FY1996 10-K states he founded it and was chairman and CEO from 1972 until 1985 (the IDCH says he started it as a research venture in 1969 and went full-time in 1972 - the two are consistent, but they give different lower bounds). It certainly crossed: by 1984 it was one of the handful of firms sharing a US pacemaker market of about $950 million and raiding Medtronic's salesforce (Circulation, 'Cardiac Pacing, 1960-1985'), and Siemens bought it in 1985 for a reported $150 million against a 1985 rev10 bar of $3,342,207. But FOUR attempts (searches for Pacesetter annual sales in 1978-1984, for the Siemens deal terms in English and German, the implantable-device.com corporate history, and Mann's SEC-filed bios) produced NO revenue figure for any year of his ownership. Bracketing from the founding to the sale gives 1972-1985, thirteen years - over the ten-year limit, and 1969-1985 is worse. So the first crossing can be neither pinned nor bounded, and the row is EXCLUDED as crossing_undatable rather than dated by the 1985 acquisition. IPO/ACQ50 FALLBACK BARRED explicitly: the frame allows it only when no earlier crossing is known, and Pacesetter's 1985 sale is a decade or more after a crossing that the market-share record makes certain. (3) MINIMED, for completeness, and this is the frustrating part: it IS datable. Its FY1996 10-K selected financial data gives net sales of $24,079,000 for 1992, 5.5 times the 1992 bar of $4,357,914, and the business dates to a 1983 first insulin pump (the IDCH says the venture began in 1979), which would make a legal 1983-1992 bound of nine years. It is not usable, because MiniMed is his THIRD or FOURTH venture and Pacesetter crossed years earlier; recording MiniMed's crossing would date the career late by roughly a decade, which is the exact defect the frame's first-crossing rule exists to prevent. a1: born 6 November 1925 in Portland, Oregon. a2: 1951 - the IDCH MannKind entry says he completed undergraduate and graduate physics at UCLA 'in 1951'; the National Academy of Engineering memorial instead says both degrees came in 1949, hence medium confidence. a3: BOUNDED 1951-1956, Technicolor, where he worked on light filters and display systems for military applications - electro-optics, the same domain as Spectrolab. Both ends are from the same source: he took the job after completing his studies (1951) and left to found Spectrolab (1956); no source dates the start month or year. a4: 1956, Spectrolab, per Mann's own bio in MiniMed's 10-K, which also confirms Heliotek in 1960 and the 1960 Textron sale of both. a6: 1985, the sale of Pacesetter Systems to Siemens (same 10-K bio; the IDCH puts the price at $150 million with about half going to Mann). MiniMed's July 1995 IPO is the alternative scale event and the first public listing of anything he founded.
